storm.summary_layperson: No storms are on radar or expected to reach the cove during this window — it should stay dry, though NWS is watching a stronger system for tomorrow.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound's marine layer is still substantial (13°F air–water gap at 5 PM) but fades to near zero by 8 PM — moot tonight since there's nothing on radar to blunt.
storm.detail_html:
Radar is clear over the cove and greater Long Island Sound this evening — KOKX shows no echoes, and no storm cells are tracked in the approach sector. A Heat Advisory remains in effect into Sunday evening (heat index near 96°F this afternoon), but that's a heat concern, not a convective one.

HRRR instability for the 17:00–22:00 window stays modest: CAPE peaks around 1,220 J/kg near 7 PM before falling off after sunset, well under the 1,500 J/kg threshold this pipeline treats as a moderate-risk trigger. Bulk shear sits near 16 kt, also below the 20 kt gate. Nothing in tonight's environment supports organized convection reaching the cove.

The OKX Area Forecast Discussion does flag a stronger system — SBCAPE 2,500–3,500 J/kg, 30–45 kt shear, and a marginal severe risk — but that's tied to a front arriving tomorrow (Aug 10), not tonight's window. Worth watching for the next publish cycle, not a factor for 17:00–22:00 today.

Because there's no storm to test it against, the cove's marine-layer protection is academic tonight. The air–water gap is a strong 13°F at 5 PM (Sound at 75°F vs air near 88°F) but decays through the evening as the land cools — it crosses below the ~5°F protective threshold around 8:07 PM and keeps falling overnight. If anything were to develop late, it would be arriving into a cove with little buffer left.

Bottom line: dry evening, low storm risk, nothing on radar to track.

wind.tactics_blurb: Despite a strong 13°F air–water gap, the sea breeze never established — this is a moderate NW gradient-wind day, not a thermal day, and it fades to drifter range by 9–10 PM. Start mid-line, favor the middle of the course away from shore-side lulls, and don't count on wind late in the window.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Despite a strong 13°F air–water temperature gap — normally plenty to build a sea breeze — the thermal never established today. Station observations show why: only 11% of coastal stations are reading any southerly component, and the near-cove cluster (RYC, Old Greenwich, Port Chester) is uniformly NW at high agreement. This is a moderate gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day — the deltaT (air-minus-water temperature gap) was favorable, but the offshore flow never let a thermal circulation set up.

RYC reads WNW 294° right now, 5.9 kt sustained (10-min average 11.1 kt) gusting to 18.5 kt — puffy, as expected for northwest flow funneling down over land. HRRR has the window starting around 8 kt at 5 PM and fading to 4–5 kt by 9–10 PM as the boundary layer stabilizes after dark, typical evening decay for a moderate-gradient day.

Direction backs slowly from WNW (~304°) toward NNW (~337°) through the window — a steady, one-way veer from nighttime drainage flow reinforcing the gradient, not a tactical oscillation. HRRR's forecast direction (302°) and current cove obs (315°) differ by only 13°, under the 15° threshold this pipeline flags — no override needed.

Cove geography for N–NW flow: offshore over land, gusty and puffy with big shifts near either shore. Best average pressure sits mid-cove, away from the immediate lee of trees and houses on the NW shore.

Racing character: starts in the 6–10 kt sweet spot with lively gusts, fades to sub-5-kt drifter range by the second half of the window. Later starts risk going light and shifty enough to threaten postponement.

data_caveats: RAP CAPE unavailable this cycle; instability supplemented from OKX AFD text (that AFD's severe-storm mentions apply to Aug 10, not tonight's window).
